comments.text:
I partially agree, but coming from someone who has been in property management for 30 years in Nevada and managing close to 400 properties with only a small team of 4 people there are definitely ways that this can be done efficiently and effectively for both sides. Here are just a few tips.I can offer to find the right property manager for your needs.

1. Find a property manager that uses outside third party vendors only. You do not want someone with an house team that can rack up false repairs or charges. Staying on that note, find a company that does not charge a markup for repairs or service fees. These are all questions that can be and should be asked up front. Also set a maintenance limit I suggest anything under $500 should be done while the vendor is on the property, anything over that amount requires owner, direct approval in writing. Make sure the property manager is providing multiple estimates if repair work is over $1000.00 this keeps the vendors that they are using competitive.

2. Make sure your property manager is doing at least annual inspections with your tenants. During the first year, I do one at the 6 month mark and then subsequently, every year at the time of lease renewal. For those that do not have HOA's I do quarterly exterior drive by's.

3. Look for someone who has not only been in the business a number of years, but those who come with also with extra credentials. I have worked in the construction field previously. I also obtained my home inspection license; therefore, i'm the one that is conducting all move in's, move-out and periodic Inspections. My owners are getting essentially a home inspection annually for their properties and not just on current items but preventative maintenance items to try and ward off the middle of the night emergency calls. They are getting a full detailed report of their homes. Any comments and suggestions with pictures.

4. We are a first come first serve property management company meaning the first person that applies online is guaranteed the property, as long as they meet our qualifications. We do not sift through multiple applications and collect fees as this is the first sign of bad business.

I have so many other tips and business requirements for my own company. But these are a few that if you decide to go with a property management company will help protect you and screen out the ones that are in it to make a quick buck and don't really care about your properties or their business.
